context.intent: Harden the local Pipeline candidate so that a silently failing bootstrap cannot leave repository write access behind, then exercise the gated push on the feature branch.
scope: Six wired hooks and the mandatory bootstrap preflight were silently disarmed by a symlinked plugin root, and are now fixed with a suite that executes them through a real symlink.
The same entrypoint defect spanned 73 plugin scripts in thirteen spellings, two of which were also broken on native Windows.
Two write paths were ungated and are now closed, the notebook editing tool that reached no matcher and the gate-strength refusal that an ordinary shell command walked around.

Still to do, restore the temporarily lifted test-path protections, bump the plugin cachebuster, run the full verify and security gates on that candidate, obtain an independent Critic review, hand over an install guide for the new local version, and finish with the signed push.
constraints: Feature branch only, with no merge to the main branch and no release.
The push gate demands a detached signature the agent cannot produce, so the human signs outside the session.
The test-path protections have no in-session override by design, so only the human can lift and restore them.
The enforcing plugin copy is deliberately separate from the checkout, so guard changes take effect only after the operator reinstalls.
questions: Whether the test-path protection should gain an audited override or be documented as human-only by design, since the standing exception currently has no mechanism behind it.
Whether the remaining shell route into the enforcing plugin root should get a second independent control rather than relying on a single guard.
